phenotype_details.name: Moderate Aldosterone Response

phenotype_details.name: Moderate Angiotensin Response

phenotype_details.name: Reduced Leptin Sensitivity
phenotype_details.description: LEPR Q223R G allele frequency: 48%. Affects leptin receptor function and satiety signaling.
phenotype_details.dietary_impact: GG genotype associated with 1.82x T2DM risk and increased energy intake. Structured eating and strict portion control critical. Monitor glucose regularly.

dietary_recommendation.recommendation: GG genotype associated with 1.82x T2DM risk and increased energy intake. Structured eating and strict portion control critical. Monitor glucose regularly.
dietary_recommendation.notes: GG homozygotes have impaired leptin signaling, leading to reduced satiety. Regular meal timing and protein-rich foods may help.

phenotype_details.name: Moderate Fat Appetite Response
phenotype_details.description: BDNF Val66Met Met allele frequency: 20%. Affects appetite regulation specifically in response to dietary fat.
phenotype_details.dietary_impact: Some increased fat appetite tendency. Moderate dietary fat, emphasize lean proteins and complex carbs.

dietary_recommendation.recommendation: Some increased fat appetite tendency. Moderate dietary fat, emphasize lean proteins and complex carbs.
dietary_recommendation.notes: BDNF Met carriers do NOT show hyperphagia on low-fat or high-sucrose diets - the effect is FAT-SPECIFIC. Low-fat diet is the targeted intervention.

phenotype_details.name: Reduced Fat Taste Sensitivity
phenotype_details.description: CD36 A allele frequency: 50%. Affects oral fat taste receptor sensitivity.
phenotype_details.dietary_impact: Higher fat detection threshold leads to unconscious fat overconsumption. Practice mindful eating, use texture modifications (crispy, creamy) to enhance satiety without excess fat.

dietary_recommendation.recommendation: Higher fat detection threshold leads to unconscious fat overconsumption. Practice mindful eating, use texture modifications (crispy, creamy) to enhance satiety without excess fat.
dietary_recommendation.notes: AA genotype (~25% Europeans) have higher fat detection thresholds. They may need to consciously track fat intake rather than relying on taste satisfaction.

phenotype_details.name: Low Plant Fat Conversion
phenotype_details.description: FADS2 insertion allele frequency: 18%. Represents positive selection for plant-to-animal fatty acid conversion in populations with long vegetarian traditions.
phenotype_details.dietary_impact: Limited ability to convert plant ALA to EPA/DHA. Rely on preformed EPA/DHA from fish, fish oil, or algae supplements rather than plant sources like flaxseed.

dietary_recommendation.recommendation: Limited ability to convert plant ALA to EPA/DHA. Rely on preformed EPA/DHA from fish, fish oil, or algae supplements rather than plant sources like flaxseed.
dietary_recommendation.notes: High converters efficiently make EPA/DHA from plants but also convert omega-6 to inflammatory arachidonic acid. Traditional South Asian diets with mustard oil and ghee are more compatible than Western vegetable oil-heavy diets.

phenotype_details.name: Evening Chronotype Risk
phenotype_details.description: CLOCK 3111C allele frequency: 30%. Affects circadian rhythm and meal timing response.
phenotype_details.dietary_impact: C allele associated with evening chronotype and increased waist-to-hip ratio. Avoid eating within 2 hours of sleep. Front-load calories to morning and afternoon.

dietary_recommendation.recommendation: C allele associated with evening chronotype and increased waist-to-hip ratio. Avoid eating within 2 hours of sleep. Front-load calories to morning and afternoon.
dietary_recommendation.notes: Evening chronotypes gain more weight from late eating. Eating the same calories earlier in the day produces better metabolic outcomes.

phenotype_details.name: High Meal Timing Response
phenotype_details.description: PER1 rs2735611 frequency: 40%. Affects response to meal timing consistency.
phenotype_details.dietary_impact: Strong responder to meal regularity. Consistent meal timing within a 1-hour daily window is especially beneficial - associated with 11.6% decrease in long-term weight gain.

dietary_recommendation.recommendation: Strong responder to meal regularity. Consistent meal timing within a 1-hour daily window is especially beneficial - associated with 11.6% decrease in long-term weight gain.
dietary_recommendation.notes: PER1 regulates circadian rhythms. High responders benefit significantly from eating at the same times daily.

phenotype_details.name: Moderate DAO Activity
phenotype_details.description: DAO rs2052129 T allele frequency: 28%. Affects diamine oxidase activity and histamine breakdown.
phenotype_details.dietary_impact: Some histamine sensitivity possible. Monitor reactions to aged/fermented foods. Moderate intake of high-histamine foods.

dietary_recommendation.recommendation: Some histamine sensitivity possible. Monitor reactions to aged/fermented foods. Moderate intake of high-histamine foods.
dietary_recommendation.notes: DAO enzyme breaks down dietary histamine. Low activity causes headaches, flushing, GI symptoms after high-histamine foods. Fresh foods are safer than aged/fermented.

phenotype_details.name: Caffeine Sensitive (Anxiety/Insomnia)
phenotype_details.description: ADORA2A rs5751876 frequency: 48%. Affects adenosine receptor sensitivity to caffeine (separate from metabolism speed).
phenotype_details.dietary_impact: TT genotype = anxiety after 100-150mg caffeine. CC genotype = caffeine-induced insomnia. Limit caffeine to <100mg/day OR avoid after noon. This is SEPARATE from CYP1A2 metabolism - you can metabolize caffeine quickly but still be sensitive.

dietary_recommendation.recommendation: TT genotype = anxiety after 100-150mg caffeine. CC genotype = caffeine-induced insomnia. Limit caffeine to <100mg/day OR avoid after noon. This is SEPARATE from CYP1A2 metabolism - you can metabolize caffeine quickly but still be sensitive.
dietary_recommendation.notes: ADORA2A affects how caffeine FEELS, not how fast you metabolize it. Even fast CYP1A2 metabolizers can be ADORA2A-sensitive and experience anxiety or insomnia from caffeine.

phenotype_details.name: Low Gout Risk
phenotype_details.description: ABCG2 rs2231142 T allele frequency: 9%. Affects uric acid transport - dysfunction leads to hyperuricemia and gout.
phenotype_details.dietary_impact: Lower genetic gout risk. Standard dietary guidelines apply.

dietary_recommendation.recommendation: Lower genetic gout risk. Standard dietary guidelines apply.
dietary_recommendation.notes: ABCG2 is a urate transporter. Dysfunction causes uric acid accumulation. Pacific Islanders and Filipinos have highest frequencies globally.

phenotype_details.name: High Urate Variant Frequency
phenotype_details.description: SLC2A9 rs734553 frequency: 75%. Affects renal urate handling. Near-fixed in Pacific Islanders (98-100%).
phenotype_details.dietary_impact: High frequency of urate-affecting variant. Good hydration and moderate purine intake recommended as baseline.

dietary_recommendation.recommendation: High frequency of urate-affecting variant. Good hydration and moderate purine intake recommended as baseline.
dietary_recommendation.notes: SLC2A9 affects how kidneys handle uric acid. Combined with ABCG2 variants, explains extremely high gout rates in Pacific Islander populations.

phenotype_details.name: General Population FH Carrier Rate

phenotype_details.dietary_impact: General population FH carrier rate. Standard lipid screening recommended. Family history of early heart disease warrants earlier screening.
phenotype_details.note: This variant has highest frequency in Ashkenazi Jewish populations (1.5% carrier rate, 1:67). Current app does not have a dedicated Ashkenazi culture, so European frequencies reflect general population rates where Ashkenazi diaspora is present.

dietary_recommendation.recommendation: General population FH carrier rate. Standard lipid screening recommended. Family history of early heart disease warrants earlier screening.
dietary_recommendation.notes: FH causes very high LDL from birth. Heterozygotes have 2-3x normal LDL. Early statin therapy dramatically reduces cardiovascular events. Diet alone is usually insufficient for FH.

phenotype_details.name: Caffeine Sensitive (Anxiety/Insomnia)

dietary_recommendation.notes: ADORA2A affects how caffeine FEELS, not how fast you metabolize it. Even fast CYP1A2 metabolizers can be ADORA2A-sensitive and experience anxiety or insomnia from caffeine.

dietary_recommendation.notes: ABCG2 is a urate transporter. Dysfunction causes uric acid accumulation. Pacific Islanders and Filipinos have highest frequencies globally.

phenotype_details.name: Moderate Plant Fat Conversion

dietary_recommendation.notes: AGTR1 mediates vasoconstriction. High activity benefits from potassium-rich foods (bananas, leafy greens, potatoes).

phenotype_details.name: Reduced Leptin Sensitivity
phenotype_details.description: LEPR Q223R G allele frequency: 47%. Affects leptin receptor function and satiety signaling.
phenotype_details.dietary_impact: GG genotype associated with 1.82x T2DM risk and increased energy intake. Structured eating and strict portion control critical. Monitor glucose regularly.

dietary_recommendation.recommendation: GG genotype associated with 1.82x T2DM risk and increased energy intake. Structured eating and strict portion control critical. Monitor glucose regularly.
dietary_recommendation.notes: GG homozygotes have impaired leptin signaling, leading to reduced satiety. Regular meal timing and protein-rich foods may help.

phenotype_details.name: Moderate Fat Appetite Response
phenotype_details.description: BDNF Val66Met Met allele frequency: 19%. Affects appetite regulation specifically in response to dietary fat.
phenotype_details.dietary_impact: Some increased fat appetite tendency. Moderate dietary fat, emphasize lean proteins and complex carbs.

dietary_recommendation.recommendation: Some increased fat appetite tendency. Moderate dietary fat, emphasize lean proteins and complex carbs.
dietary_recommendation.notes: BDNF Met carriers do NOT show hyperphagia on low-fat or high-sucrose diets - the effect is FAT-SPECIFIC. Low-fat diet is the targeted intervention.

phenotype_details.name: Reduced Fat Taste Sensitivity
phenotype_details.description: CD36 A allele frequency: 51%. Affects oral fat taste receptor sensitivity.
phenotype_details.dietary_impact: Higher fat detection threshold leads to unconscious fat overconsumption. Practice mindful eating, use texture modifications (crispy, creamy) to enhance satiety without excess fat.

dietary_recommendation.recommendation: Higher fat detection threshold leads to unconscious fat overconsumption. Practice mindful eating, use texture modifications (crispy, creamy) to enhance satiety without excess fat.
dietary_recommendation.notes: AA genotype (~25% Europeans) have higher fat detection thresholds. They may need to consciously track fat intake rather than relying on taste satisfaction.

phenotype_details.name: Low Plant Fat Conversion
phenotype_details.description: FADS2 insertion allele frequency: 17%. Represents positive selection for plant-to-animal fatty acid conversion in populations with long vegetarian traditions.
phenotype_details.dietary_impact: Limited ability to convert plant ALA to EPA/DHA. Rely on preformed EPA/DHA from fish, fish oil, or algae supplements rather than plant sources like flaxseed.

dietary_recommendation.recommendation: Limited ability to convert plant ALA to EPA/DHA. Rely on preformed EPA/DHA from fish, fish oil, or algae supplements rather than plant sources like flaxseed.
dietary_recommendation.notes: High converters efficiently make EPA/DHA from plants but also convert omega-6 to inflammatory arachidonic acid. Traditional South Asian diets with mustard oil and ghee are more compatible than Western vegetable oil-heavy diets.

phenotype_details.name: Evening Chronotype Risk
phenotype_details.description: CLOCK 3111C allele frequency: 31%. Affects circadian rhythm and meal timing response.
phenotype_details.dietary_impact: C allele associated with evening chronotype and increased waist-to-hip ratio. Avoid eating within 2 hours of sleep. Front-load calories to morning and afternoon.

dietary_recommendation.recommendation: C allele associated with evening chronotype and increased waist-to-hip ratio. Avoid eating within 2 hours of sleep. Front-load calories to morning and afternoon.
dietary_recommendation.notes: Evening chronotypes gain more weight from late eating. Eating the same calories earlier in the day produces better metabolic outcomes.

phenotype_details.name: High Meal Timing Response
phenotype_details.description: PER1 rs2735611 frequency: 39%. Affects response to meal timing consistency.
phenotype_details.dietary_impact: Strong responder to meal regularity. Consistent meal timing within a 1-hour daily window is especially beneficial - associated with 11.6% decrease in long-term weight gain.

dietary_recommendation.recommendation: Strong responder to meal regularity. Consistent meal timing within a 1-hour daily window is especially beneficial - associated with 11.6% decrease in long-term weight gain.
dietary_recommendation.notes: PER1 regulates circadian rhythms. High responders benefit significantly from eating at the same times daily.

phenotype_details.name: Moderate DAO Activity
phenotype_details.description: DAO rs2052129 T allele frequency: 27%. Affects diamine oxidase activity and histamine breakdown.
phenotype_details.dietary_impact: Some histamine sensitivity possible. Monitor reactions to aged/fermented foods. Moderate intake of high-histamine foods.

dietary_recommendation.recommendation: Some histamine sensitivity possible. Monitor reactions to aged/fermented foods. Moderate intake of high-histamine foods.
dietary_recommendation.notes: DAO enzyme breaks down dietary histamine. Low activity causes headaches, flushing, GI symptoms after high-histamine foods. Fresh foods are safer than aged/fermented.

phenotype_details.name: Caffeine Sensitive (Anxiety/Insomnia)
phenotype_details.description: ADORA2A rs5751876 frequency: 46%. Affects adenosine receptor sensitivity to caffeine (separate from metabolism speed).
phenotype_details.dietary_impact: TT genotype = anxiety after 100-150mg caffeine. CC genotype = caffeine-induced insomnia. Limit caffeine to <100mg/day OR avoid after noon. This is SEPARATE from CYP1A2 metabolism - you can metabolize caffeine quickly but still be sensitive.

dietary_recommendation.recommendation: TT genotype = anxiety after 100-150mg caffeine. CC genotype = caffeine-induced insomnia. Limit caffeine to <100mg/day OR avoid after noon. This is SEPARATE from CYP1A2 metabolism - you can metabolize caffeine quickly but still be sensitive.
dietary_recommendation.notes: ADORA2A affects how caffeine FEELS, not how fast you metabolize it. Even fast CYP1A2 metabolizers can be ADORA2A-sensitive and experience anxiety or insomnia from caffeine.

phenotype_details.name: Low Gout Risk
phenotype_details.description: ABCG2 rs2231142 T allele frequency: 9%. Affects uric acid transport - dysfunction leads to hyperuricemia and gout.
phenotype_details.dietary_impact: Lower genetic gout risk. Standard dietary guidelines apply.

dietary_recommendation.recommendation: Lower genetic gout risk. Standard dietary guidelines apply.
dietary_recommendation.notes: ABCG2 is a urate transporter. Dysfunction causes uric acid accumulation. Pacific Islanders and Filipinos have highest frequencies globally.

phenotype_details.name: High Urate Variant Frequency
phenotype_details.description: SLC2A9 rs734553 frequency: 75%. Affects renal urate handling. Near-fixed in Pacific Islanders (98-100%).
phenotype_details.dietary_impact: High frequency of urate-affecting variant. Good hydration and moderate purine intake recommended as baseline.

dietary_recommendation.recommendation: High frequency of urate-affecting variant. Good hydration and moderate purine intake recommended as baseline.
dietary_recommendation.notes: SLC2A9 affects how kidneys handle uric acid. Combined with ABCG2 variants, explains extremely high gout rates in Pacific Islander populations.

phenotype_details.name: General Population FH Carrier Rate
phenotype_details.description: LDLR G197del carrier frequency: 0.3%. Causes familial hypercholesterolemia (FH).
phenotype_details.dietary_impact: General population FH carrier rate. Standard lipid screening recommended. Family history of early heart disease warrants earlier screening.
phenotype_details.note: This variant has highest frequency in Ashkenazi Jewish populations (1.5% carrier rate, 1:67). Current app does not have a dedicated Ashkenazi culture, so European frequencies reflect general population rates where Ashkenazi diaspora is present.

dietary_recommendation.recommendation: General population FH carrier rate. Standard lipid screening recommended. Family history of early heart disease warrants earlier screening.
dietary_recommendation.notes: FH causes very high LDL from birth. Heterozygotes have 2-3x normal LDL. Early statin therapy dramatically reduces cardiovascular events. Diet alone is usually insufficient for FH.
